After FDR correction, the differences in eight HRV parameters between fatigue groups remained significant (all q < 0.05), whereas the differences between sleep-quality groups did not survive correction. Our findings suggest that alterations in HRV parameters, particularly mean heart rate (MeanHR) and acceleration capacity (AC), are associated with the severity of fatigue and sleep disturbances in HCC patients. Given the exploratory cross-sectional design, these metrics should be regarded as candidate non-invasive physiological correlates of autonomic dysfunction and symptom burden. Their clinical relevance requires confirmation in larger prospective studies.

papers.title: Applications of functional ultrasound brain-computer interfaces in neurological diseases: research progress based on neurovascular coupling.
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) bypass peripheral nerves and muscles to establish direct information pathways between the brain and external devices, providing novel approaches for motor function reconstruction, communication assistance, and neurorehabilitation in patients with neurological disorders. However, conventional non-invasive BCIs relying on modalities such as electroencephalography (EEG), magnetoencephalography (MEG), or functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) exhibit limitations in spatiotemporal resolution, portability, or real-time capability. Functional ultrasound (fUS), an emerging neuroimaging technology based on neurovascular coupling (NVC), detects cerebral blood volume changes at a spatial resolution of approximately 100 μm; its imaging frame interval is 200-500 ms, whereas its effective temporal resolution, limited by the hemodynamic response, is 1-2 s, offering a potential solution to overcome these constraints. This review comprehensively analyzed NVC-based fUS brain-computer interfaces from the dimensions of technical principles, clinical applications, future directions, and challenges. fUS has demonstrated significant clinical value in stroke assessment, epilepsy monitoring, and early identification of neurodegenerative diseases. Emerging technologies such as transcranial focused ultrasound neuromodulation, sonogenetics, and intravascular ultrasound are driving the evolution of fUS from single-signal "acquisition" toward bidirectional "acquisition-modulation" closed-loop systems, which remain at the proof-of-concept stage. However, the hemodynamic response latency relative to neural electrical activity (1-2 s), the yet-unclear biosafety of chronic ultrasound exposure, and insufficient decoding reliability under pathological conditions remain critical bottlenecks requiring urgent resolution. In conclusion, NVC-based fUS brain-computer interfaces provide a novel tool for precision diagnosis and treatment of neurological diseases. Future efforts should focus on conducting multicenter clinical trials and enhancing the robustness of decoding algorithms.

papers.title: A bimodal deep learning framework for cerebral perfusion assessment using synchronous ECG and near-field coupled CBF signals.
papers.abstract: Accurate real-time assessment of cerebral blood flow (CBF) is crucial for optimizing treatment decisions and improving prognostic outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS). In this study, leveraging the advantage of near-field coupling (NFC) technology in capturing blood flow information from intracranial vessels of different sizes, and in combination with synchronous ECG signals reflecting cardiac rhythm fluctuations, we propose a bimodal deep learning framework to characterize cerebral perfusion-related state changes under postural tilt using synchronous ECG and NFC-based CBF (NFC-CBF) signals. The framework consists of a Multi-Scale Feature Extractor (MSFE) and a Depthwise-Separable Cross-Attention Fusion (DSCAF) module, which work collaboratively to achieve hierarchical temporal representation learning and cross-modal fusion of ECG and NFC-CBF signals. Using synchronous ECG and NFC-CBF data collected from young and middle-aged healthy volunteers, we evaluated the proposed framework in binary and four-class classification tasks to assess its feasibility for cerebral perfusion-related state classification. The results show that NFC-CBF signals can capture CBF changes before and after tilt. Synchronous monitoring of ECG and NFC-CBF provided complementary information on cardiac rhythm and cerebral perfusion-related dynamics. The proposed framework outperforms Bimodal Feature Fusion, ResNet-SE-LSTM, and Cross-Transformer Network in terms of accuracy, F1-score, specificity, precision, and recall, achieving accuracies of 95.95% ± 1.54% and 79.29% ± 2.12% in the binary posture classification and four-class age-posture classification tasks, respectively. Ablation experiments indicate that bimodal modeling provided additional discriminative information compared with single-modality inputs, particularly for the four-class task involving both posture and age. The classification performance achieved after incorporating the DSCAF module is superior to that of other conventional feature fusion strategies. These findings support the feasibility of bimodal ECG and NFC-CBF modeling for cerebral perfusion-related state classification under postural perturbation, while further validation in larger, more diverse, and demographically balanced cohorts, including both patient and non-patient populations, is required before its clinical applicability can be established.

papers.title: Latent Transition Analysis of Symptom Burden Before and After Pulmonary Rehabilitation in Postoperative Lung Cancer Patients.
papers.abstract: To identify latent classes of symptom burden in lung cancer patients before and after pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) and to examine factors associated with transitions between classes. A longitudinal study. The M. D. Anderson Symptom Inventory (Chinese version) was completed by 273 postoperative lung cancer patients before (T1) and 12 weeks after PR (T2). Latent profile analysis identified symptom burden classes, and latent transition analysis estimated the probability of moving between classes. Measurement invariance was tested, and the two-class solution was retained on the basis of fit indices, entropy and interpretability. Univariate-significant variables entered a logistic regression model. Two latent classes were identified at both T1 and T2 (high and low symptom burden). The two-class solution was retained because it showed the lowest AIC, BIC and aBIC, adequate entropy (0.844 at T1; 0.902 at T2) and interpretable profiles, whereas the three-class model did not improve fit and yielded small classes. Among 262 patients (95.97% valid), the low burden class was stable (0.863), and 61.07% of patients in the high burden class at T1 moved to the low burden class at T2; these probabilities denote the proportion of patients moving between classes. Age <45 years (OR = 2.345), no financial burden (OR = 2.841), satisfactory sleep (OR = 3.130) and family living (OR = 2.949) were associated with transition from the high to the low burden class, whereas age ≥60 years (OR = 0.724), unmarried (OR = 0.418) and divorced (OR = 0.405) status with lower odds of transition. Symptom burden in postoperative lung cancer patients is heterogeneous and follows class-specific trajectories. Younger age, better sleep and stronger family and financial resources were associated with a favourable transition. As this was a single-arm observational study, the findings indicate associations rather than causal effects of PR.

papers.title: Protein supplementation and resistance training-induced strength gains in young adults: a meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to determine whether protein supplementation confers additional benefits for muscle strength gains beyond those induced by resistance training (RT) alone in healthy young adults. A systematic literature search was performed in PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and SPORTDiscus through April 1, 2026. Twenty-three randomized controlled trials involving 611 healthy young adults were included. Pooled estimates were calculated as weighted mean differences (WMD) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using a random-effects model. Subgroup analysis, meta-regression, and leave-one-out and leave-one-category-out sensitivity analysis were performed to explore heterogeneity. Compared with RT alone, combined RT and protein supplementation produced significant improvements in both bench press (WMD: 2.63 kg, 95% CI: 0.77-4.49, p = 0.006) and squat strength (WMD: 7.40 kg, 95% CI: 2.15-12.66, p = 0.006). Subgroup analysis revealed that the ergogenic effect on squat strength was predominantly observed when the intervention lasted ≤12 weeks, or when protein was ingested both around exercise (pre- and/or post-exercise) and before sleep. Meta-regression identified intervention duration as a significant moderator (p = 0.037) and protein timing as a borderline moderator (p = 0.073) of squat strength heterogeneity. Sensitivity analysis showed that the pooled effects remained significant and consistent in direction. Protein supplementation combined with resistance training enhances muscle strength in young healthy adults, but its incremental benefit appears conditional on intervention duration, nutrient timing, training background, and baseline protein status rather than universally applicable. Future well-powered trials with standardized protein dose and source reporting, repeated measures of habitual protein intake, and stratified designs are needed to clarify these interactions and support more personalized, mechanism-informed exercise and nutrition guidance. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/# myprospero, PROSPERO, identifier: CRD42024534481.

papers.title: Functional changes during inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation in Poland: an ICF-based analysis of functioning relevant to healthy aging and public health.
papers.abstract: The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) provides a comprehensive framework for assessing rehabilitation outcomes beyond traditional physiological measures. This retrospective observational study used a longitudinal pre-post design and involved a secondary analysis of anonymized data collected during a national pilot implementation of an ICF-based functional assessment system in routine Polish rehabilitation services It aimed to characterize within-patient changes in functioning observed between admission and discharge among 100 adults undergoing inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation, with a mean age of 68.7 ± 10.8 years (with 75% in the ≥65 years group), at baseline and 2-3 weeks post-rehabilitation. Changes in ICF qualifiers for Body Functions (B), Activities and Participation (D), and Environmental Factors (E) were evaluated using paired comparisons. At baseline, the greatest impairments were observed in energy and drive functions (b130), sleep functions (b134), pain (b280), exercise tolerance functions (b455), joint mobility (b710), muscle power (b730), muscle endurance (b740), changing basic body position (d410), maintaining a body position (d415), and walking (d450). Between admission and discharge, significant reductions in impairment severity were observed in several body function categories, including muscle power (median qualifier 3 → 1), muscle endurance (3 → 2), joint mobility (3 → 1), pain (b280), exercise tolerance (1 → 0), and sensations associated with cardiovascular and respiratory functions (2 → 1) (all adjusted p < 0.01). Significant reductions in activity limitations were also observed for changing basic body position (3 → 2), maintaining a body position (3 → 2), walking (2 → 1), transfers (severe/complete limitation: 17% → 4%), daily routines (severe/complete limitation: 36% → 19%), and multiple self-care activities multiple self-care activities, including washing (1 → 0), caring for body parts (1 → 0), toileting (severe/complete limitation: 2% → 0%), and dressing (1 → 0) (all adjusted p < 0.01). Environmental factors remained stable, with medications, assistive products and technologies and family support consistently identified as facilitators of functioning. These findings describe differences across several dimensions of ICF-rated functioning between admission and discharge during inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation. They suggest that routine ICF-based assessments may provide a useful multidimensional description of functioning. Future controlled studies could examine the extent to which these differences are attributable to rehabilitation, while dedicated validation studies could assess the responsiveness of the ICF-based assessment system and the clinical meaning of changes in qualifier scores.

papers.title: Latent profiles of 24-h movement behaviors and bone health at one-year follow-up in Chinese preschool children.
papers.abstract: Physical activity, sedentary behavior and sleep together occupy a fixed 24-h day, yet their relation to bone health in early childhood has largely been examined one behavior at a time, or through adherence to separate guideline thresholds. Person-centred approaches that characterise the whole-day composition have not been applied to bone health in preschool children. A total of 109 children (mean age 4.33 years; 44.0% girls) from three kindergartens in Changsha, China, were followed for 1 year. Sedentary behavior, light and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity were measured by hip-worn accelerometry over seven consecutive days, and sleep was reported daily by parents and recorded by class teachers including the weekend days. The four behaviors were closed to 1,440 min/day, expressed as isometric log-ratio coordinates, and summarised by latent profile analysis. Bone health was indexed by the tibial speed of sound (SOS) from quantitative ultrasound, expressed as a z-score for age, sex and ethnicity. Covariates were related to profile membership by the bias-adjusted three-step approach, and profiles to the SOS z-score by the Bolck-Croon-Hagenaars approach in baseline score and 1-year follow-up score models. Three profiles were identified: Sedentary (n = 31), Low-active, long-sleeping (n = 7) and Active (n = 71). Older children were more likely to belong to the Active profile than to the Sedentary profile (OR 2.164 per year, 95% CI 1.012 to 4.630), whereas sex, socioeconomic status score and body mass index z-score were not associated with profile membership. At baseline the SOS z-score did not differ across profiles. At 1-year follow-up, children in the Active profile scored lower than those in the Sedentary profile (adjusted difference -0.462, 95% CI -0.774 to -0.150, p = 0.004, Holm-adjusted p = 0.016), whereas the Low-active, long-sleeping profile did not differ (-0.256, 95% CI -0.844 to 0.332). An association between 24-h movement profile membership and bone health was present at 1-year follow-up but not at baseline. The whole-day movement composition therefore merits consideration in bone health research and promotion in the preschool years.

papers.title: Serotonergic regulation of neuronal excitability and glutamatergic synaptic transmission in rat claustrum.
papers.abstract: The claustrum (CLA) receives dense serotonergic innervation from dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) serotonin (5-HT) neurons, which are implicated in regulating sleep and stress homeostasis. However, the mechanisms by which 5-HT regulates the excitability of CLA neurons remain poorly defined. In the present study, we combined whole-cell patch-clamp recordings, 5-HT uncaging, and receptor pharmacology to examine the effects of 5-HT on the excitability of CLA neurons and their glutamatergic synapses. We found that 5-HT consistently induced membrane hyperpolarization or depolarization in regular-spiking type I and type II neurons, whereas it predominantly induced hyperpolarization in strongly adapting CLA neurons. The 5-HT-induced membrane hyperpolarization and depolarization were mediated by 5-HT1A receptors (5-HT1ARs) and 5-HT2A receptors (5-HT2ARs), respectively. Furthermore, we showed that activation of presynaptic 5-HT2ARs inhibits glutamatergic synaptic transmission in the CLA by reducing glutamate release. This effect was not mediated by the canonical phospholipase C (PLC) signaling cascade. Collectively, these findings reveal cell type-specific and multifaceted serotonergic modulation of the intrinsic excitability and synaptic transmission in the claustrum.

papers.title: Cognitive workload across subjective and electrodermal measures in relation to previous-night sleep.
papers.abstract: Cognitive workload is commonly assessed using both subjective and physiological indicators, although these measures may reflect different aspects of task-related strain. Sleep duration may further modify perceived task demand without producing proportional changes in physiological activation. This study examined the association between perceived cognitive workload and electrodermal task reactivity, and explored whether previous-night short sleep was associated with higher subjective workload without increased electrodermal activation. A total of 52 adults were initially assessed; two were excluded due to violation of predefined eligibility criteria, resulting in a final analytical sample of 50 participants. Participants reported previous-night sleep duration and subjective sleep quality, completed a 5-min resting baseline, and then performed the Determination Test from the Vienna Test System. Electrodermal activity was recorded continuously during baseline and task performance, while perceived workload was assessed after the task using the NASA Task Load Index. Task-related electrodermal reactivity was calculated as GSR task-baseline difference, and participants were classified into short-sleep (< 7 h) and normal-sleep (≥7 h) groups. NASA-TLX total workload was not significantly associated with GSR task-baseline difference (rho = 0.126, p = 0.383). In the uncorrected threshold-based comparison, participants with short sleep reported higher perceived workload than those with normal sleep (64.44 ± 8.31 vs. 58.70 ± 9.57; p = 0.027), whereas GSR task-baseline difference was nearly identical between groups (4.57 ± 2.19 vs. 4.61 ± 2.93 μS; p = 0.884). However, the workload difference did not survive FDR correction across exploratory subgroup comparisons and should therefore be interpreted as a nominal finding. Overall, perceived workload and electrodermal reactivity showed limited correspondence, whereas the sleep-related analyses did not provide consistent evidence of an association with either outcome.

papers.title: Computational approaches to deep learning-driven EEG analysis for neurological disease diagnosis: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a widely used non-invasive neurophysiological technique for analyzing brain dynamics and diagnosing neurological diseases. However, the non-stationary nature, low signal-to-noise ratio, and inter-subject variability of EEG signals cause significant challenges to traditional analytical approaches. In recent years, deep learning has emerged as a powerful computational tool for EEG analysis, which enables automated feature learning and improved diagnostic accuracy with minimal human-driven feature extraction. This review systematically explains computational approaches in deep learning-driven EEG analysis for the diagnosis of neurological diseases. It includes recent advances in deep learning architectures, such as convolutional neural networks (CNN), recurrent neural networks (RNN), hybrid configurations, Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), Large Language Models (LLM), autoencoders, and transformer-based models, with a focus on their capacity to model spatial, temporal, and spatiotemporal dynamics in EEG signals. This is applicable in diagnosing major neurological disorders such as Epilepsy, Alzheimer's disease (AD), Encephalopathy, Parkinson's disease (PD), Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), sleep disorders, and developmental brain disorders. Furthermore, we discuss essential preprocessing strategies and denoising techniques, showing how removing biological artifacts prevents diagnostic models from confusing noise with actual signs of disease. Key challenges such as limited data availability, lack of model interpretability, inter-subject variability, and difficulty in clinical translation are identified and critically discussed. Finally, key emerging trends and future research directions are identified to support the development of clinical applications of EEG-based disease diagnostic systems.

papers.title: Body mass index, diabetes, inflammation and survival in COVID-19: a retrospective study evaluating the obesity paradox in an urban hospital center.
papers.abstract: Severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is associated with increased morbidity and mortality, particularly among patients with comorbidities such as diabetes and obesity. The combined influence of glycemic control, hyperglycemia, and body mass index (BMI) on disease severity remains incompletely understood, particularly in underserved urban populations. This retrospective study evaluated 478 adults hospitalized with confirmed COVID-19 between March and May 2020 at an urban academic medical center to examine the impact of diabetes, glycemic control, and body mass index (BMI) on clinical outcomes. Data collected included demographics, comorbidities, BMI, diabetes type, baseline hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), inflammatory markers, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, mechanical ventilation, hyperglycemia, and glucocorticoid use. Among patients with available HbA1c measurements, those with diabetes who developed cytokine storm had significantly higher mean HbA1c than those without cytokine storm. Obesity and overweight were highly prevalent, with 45% of patients classified as obese (BMI ≥30 kg/m²) and 29% classified as overweight (BMI 25-29 kg/m²). Diabetes was associated with increased ICU admission, mechanical ventilation, and steroid-induced hyperglycemia. Mortality was higher among older patients, Black patients, and those with diabetes, hypertension, hyperglycemia, greater glucocorticoid use, or ICU admission. Notably, patients with overweight or obesity demonstrated improved survival compared with those of normal weight, consistent with an obesity paradox in this urban cohort. Multivariable analysis identified steroid-induced hyperglycemia, obstructive sleep apnea, and higher methylprednisolone use as independent predictors of ICU admission, whereas higher BMI was associated with a lower risk of adverse outcomes. Diabetes and hyperglycemia were associated with greater COVID-19 severity, increased ICU utilization, and higher mortality, while higher BMI offered potential survival benefits. These findings highlight the complex interplay between metabolic dysfunction, obesity, and COVID-19 outcomes, suggesting the presence of an obesity paradox in hospitalized patients, and emphasize the importance of early recognition and management of diabetes and hyperglycemia to improve clinical outcomes.
papers.journal: Frontiers in clinical diabetes and healthcare

papers.title: Mammalian torpor and depressive disorders: a review of evidence for a connection.
papers.abstract: Unexpected similarities exist between animal torpor and depressive disorders. We examine them from a variety of perspectives and propose that these two seemingly disparate entities are related in important ways. In the animal kingdom, torpor - a hypometabolic state during which physiological functions are severely decreased - is now understood to be a response to stress, whether unanticipated or seasonal. It is used by mammals from the tropics to the poles, including by several species of primates. Humankind evolved from mammals that used torpor, and the genetic legacy enabling the torpor response exists in every person's genome. Strikingly, severe cold has occasionally created a torpor-like state in human beings - and 'synthetic hibernation' is now being studied as a modality to facilitate space travel. The expression of torpor can vary wildly among species and even between any two individuals within the same species living in the same locale, implying unusual mutability of this complex and variegated adaptation and the likely expression of aspects of it in vulnerable members of our own species. Both torpors and depressions require perturbation of the circadian clock, which is resynchronized upon recovery. The same types of prominent but reversible hippocampal changes mark both depressions and torpors. The circannual clock that drives seasonal torpors also appears to guide some recurrent affective disorders. Mammals can be brought out of their torpors by the same interventions that bring people out of their depressions. Affective catatonias and certain subtypes of depressions display aspects of a torpor-like response and are explored. Torpor arguably is the only animal model of depression that fulfills Willner's triad of face, construct, and predictive validity (plus etiological similarity, a criterion added later). Some aspects of depressive disorders, puzzling at first, can be explained if one views them from the perspective of a torpor response. Ideas for future research that might elucidate the connections between depressive disorders and torpor are suggested. The proposed connection between torpor and certain subtypes of depressive disorders warrants greater attention by researchers in these currently disconnected fields. A collaborative approach could lead to better treatments for depressed persons.

papers.title: Ekbom Spectrum Psychosis Associated with 24-hour Continuous Subcutaneous Foslevodopa/Foscarbidopa Infusion in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.abstract: Continuous subcutaneous foslevodopa/foscarbidopa infusion (CSFLI) is an emerging treatment for advanced Parkinson's disease (PD). We report atypical psychosis with Ekbom-like somatic hallucinations during CSFLI. A 74-year-old man with a 16-year history of PD (Hoehn and Yahr stage 3), mild cognitive impairment (Montreal Cognitive Assessment 25/30), and previous mild dopamine agonist-induced visual hallucinations received CSFLI for disabling motor fluctuations, dyskinesias, nocturnal rigidity, and severe morning akinesia inadequately controlled by oral therapy. Initial treatment was well tolerated, reducing OFF time, dyskinesias, and sleep disturbance. Because of recurrent motor fluctuations and nocturnal akinesia, infusion parameters were progressively increased to a daytime base rate of 0.48 ml/h and a nocturnal low-rate of 0.38 ml/h, corresponding to an estimated levodopa equivalent daily dose of approximately 1,868 mg/day. Seventy-two hours after ciprofloxacin initiation for an infected subcutaneous nodule, the patient developed vivid visual hallucinations that evolved into Ekbom-like somatic hallucinations, described as worms moving beneath the skin, leading to superficial self-inflicted lacerations. Orientation remained preserved and no delirium features were observed. Initial reduction of infusion parameters, safinamide discontinuation, and quetiapine produced only partial benefit. A subsequent selective reduction of the nocturnal low-rate from 0.36 to 0.30 ml/h was associated with a clinically meaningful reduction in psychotic symptoms, although residual hallucinations and worsening morning akinesia persisted. This case suggests that psychosis during CSFLI may reflect the interaction between neuropsychiatric vulnerability, ciprofloxacin exposure, and sustained nocturnal dopaminergic stimulation. Although causality cannot be inferred, careful nocturnal titration may help clinicians recognize and manage atypical psychotic manifestations early in susceptible patients.
papers.journal: Clinical psychopharmacology and neuroscience : the official scientific journal of the Korean College of Neuropsychopharmacology

papers.title: Predicting Polysomnography‑derived Sleep Efficiency and Total Sleep Time Using Clinical Questionnaires: A Machine Learning Approach.
papers.abstract: We developed and evaluated machine learning models to predict polysomnography (PSG)-derived sleep efficiency and total sleep time using clinical questionnaire-based assessments, with the aim of developing accessible non-invasive screening tools that can estimate objective sleep parameters in the absence of PSG. Predictive models were developed using demographic data and nine validated questionnaires from 1,135 participants. Three gradient boosting algorithms-Categorical Boosting (CatBoost), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LGBM), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost)-were compared for binary classification of sleep efficiency (≥ 85% vs. < 85%) and four-class prediction of total sleep time (< 5, 5-7, 7-9, and ≥ 9 hours). Model performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and precision-recall curve (PRC) metrics. CatBoost consistently outperformed LGBM and XGBoost. For sleep efficiency classification classification, CatBoost achieved the highest performance (AUC = 0.7342; PRC = 0.6957). In total sleep time prediction, CatBoost demonstrated superior accuracy (weighted AUC = 0.6772; weighted PRC = 0.5384; micro-AUC = 0.8195). Inclusion of formal sleep disorder diagnoses provided negligible improvements. Validated self-report instruments effectively captured clinically meaningful determinants of sleep efficiency and total sleep time. Machine learning models, particularly CatBoost, demonstrated robust performance using questionnaire-derived features alone, highlighting the central roles of age, insomnia severity, and daytime sleepiness. These findings support the feasibility and clinical utility of accessible, questionnaire-driven machine learning approaches for large-scale screening, early risk stratification, and decision support in sleep medicine.
papers.journal: Clinical psychopharmacology and neuroscience : the official scientific journal of the Korean College of Neuropsychopharmacology

papers.title: EXPRESS: Multidomain determinants of perivascular spaces indicate early cerebrovascular vulnerability in individuals at risk of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Perivascular spaces (PVS) are MRI-visible markers of cerebrovascular and glymphatic function, but their regional determinants in preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD), regarding sex and AD biomarkers, remain poorly understood. We studied 1,199 cognitively unimpaired ALFA study participants (aged 54-65 years), genetically enriched for AD risk, with CSF biomarker phenotyping in 296 participants. PVS were automatically quantified in basal ganglia, centrum semiovale, hippocampus, and midbrain on 3T MRI. Counts were modelled using Poisson or negative binomial regression, adjusting for demographics, cardiometabolic, lifestyle, and genetic factors, with effect modification by sex and amyloid/tau (AT) status. PVS showed marked regional specificity. Centrum semiovale PVS were associated with age, male sex, and cardiometabolic factors, whereas hippocampal and midbrain PVS were more closely related to AD biomarker status and sleep or psychological measures. Men exhibited higher centrum semiovale burden while women showed higher counts in hippocampus, midbrain, and basal ganglia. Associations were stronger in amyloid-positive individuals with concurrent tau pathology. Polygenic scores for lipid and metabolic traits contributed modestly to regional PVS variation. PVS burden is associated with multidomain determinants in preclinical AD with regional, sex-specific, and biomarker-dependent patterns, supporting PVS as accessible MRI markers for risk stratification and precision prevention.
papers.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism

papers.title: Patient Experiences of Chronic Low Back Pain: Development of a Conceptual Model Based on a Targeted Literature Review and Qualitative Patient Interviews.
papers.abstract: Chronic low back pain (CLBP) is a persistent, debilitating condition. The United States (US) Food and Drug Administration Patient-Focused Drug Development Guidance recommends using patient-reported outcome (PRO) measures to assess pain and function in clinical trials and document content validity of the measures based on patient experience data. The objective of this study was to explore and document the patient experience of symptoms and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) impacts of CLBP based on a targeted literature review (TLR) and qualitative patient interviews to facilitate future PRO validation studies. A TLR of patient-focused studies and qualitative interviews (N = 30) with adults with CLBP in the US were conducted to document the patient perspective of CLBP symptoms and HRQoL impacts. Results were combined in a patient-centred conceptual model. Merged results from the TLR and qualitative interviews demonstrated that adults with CLBP described highly impactful experiences of pain. The conceptual model grouped 16 symptom and 120 impact concepts. CLBP was described as commonly co-occurring with numbness, muscle spasms, and stiffness. CLBP-related HRQoL impacts included physical functioning, emotional functioning, adaptive behaviours, sleep, social functioning, household chores/responsibilities, and work/school. The findings highlight the multidimensional burden of living with CLBP. The newly developed patient-centred conceptual model may be used to explore the content validity of PRO measures and promote a robust understanding of the patient experience with CLBP. Findings suggest that utilising HRQoL endpoints and patient-centred approaches in CLBP studies of novel therapies may be an important way to quantify meaningfully effective treatments.

papers.title: Health and Care Characteristics of Ageing Adults With Profound Intellectual and Multiple Disabilities Living in French Facilities.
papers.abstract: Life expectancy among individuals with Profound Intellectual and Multiple Disabilities/Polyhandicap (PIMD/PLH) has increased, making information essential for age-appropriate care. This study compared health characteristics and care use between younger and older adults with PIMD/PLH in institutions. This cross-sectional study used data from the French PIMD/PLH cohort. Inclusion criteria were (i) age > 3 years; (ii) PIMD/PLH diagnosis. Data on health characteristics and health care consumption were included. Adults were compared by age (≤ 45 vs. > 45 years). Mean age was 34.5 ± 6.0 in the younger group and 55 ± 5.9 in the older group. While overall polyhandicap severity was similar, older adults exhibited a greater dependency level. Gastroesophageal reflux and symptomatic osteoporosis were more prevalent in the younger group; dental disorders, chronic pain, and sleep disorders predominated in the older group. Older adults received less medical and paramedical care. This study highlights the need for lifelong medical and rehabilitative care in PIMD/PLH. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT02400528.
papers.journal: Journal of applied research in intellectual disabilities : JARID

papers.title: Longitudinal Real-Time Quaking-Induced Conversion Analysis of Misfolded α-Synuclein in Idiopathic Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder Patients with Baseline Cerebrospinal Fluid Negativity.
papers.abstract: While most patients with idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder (IRBD) show CSF misfolded α-synucleinpositivity, a subset tests negative with an uncertain underlying substrate that may include non-synucleinopathy conditions. We performed a longitudinal study in polysomnography-confirmed IRBD patients with negative CSF α-synuclein at baseline (LP1) who underwent a second lumbar puncture (LP2). α-synuclein presence was determined by seed amplification assay. Among 43 αSyn -negative patients at LP1, 9 (20.9%) converted to αSyn positivity over a mean follow-up of 2.8 ± 2.3 years. At LP1, converters exhibited a higher burden of Parkinson's disease biomarkers, including hyposmia, abnormal dopamine transporter single-photon emission computed tomography (DAT-SPECT), and increased REM sleep electromyographic activity, compared with patients with persistent αSyn negativity. Longer intervals between LP1 and LP2 were associated with higher αSyn shifting to positivity. Serial CSF αSyn assessments may identify a very early synucleinopathy stage. This strategy may improve patient selection for disease-modifying trials targeting αSyn. © 2026 International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.
papers.journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society

papers.title: Impact of total hip arthroplasty on multidimensional functioning and sleep in patients with hip osteoarthritis: A prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: BackgroundTotal hip arthroplasty (THA) is an established intervention for managing advanced osteoarthritis, offering substantial improvements in pain relief. However, relationship between sleep quality and functional outcomes after THA remains underexplored.ObjectiveThis longitudinal study aimed to evaluate changes in nocturnal sleep quality and daytime sleepiness and their association with functional recovery in 55 patients undergoing primary THA.MethodsPatients undergoing primary THA were enrolled in this prospective cohort study. Nocturnal sleep quality, daytime sleepiness, functional outcomes, and health-related quality of life were assessed preoperatively and at one, three, and sixxs months postoperatively using the PSQI, ESS, WOMAC, HOOS, and SF-36. Statistical analyses included Friedman's test with post-hoc Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and Kendall's tau correlations.ResultsWOMAC, PSQI, all HOOS dimensions, and both SF-36 components significantly improved over time. PSQI scores significantly decreased from the preoperative assessment to the postoperative follow-ups, indicating improved nocturnal sleep quality. In contrast, the median ESS score was 5 at each assessment, and no statistically significant group-level change in ESS was detected (p = 0.996). WOMAC and ESS were significantly correlated at one and six months, suggesting an association between functional recovery and daytime sleepiness at these timepoints.ConclusionsTHA was associated with significant improvements in pain, function, health-related quality of life, and nocturnal sleep quality up to six months postoperatively. No statistically significant group-level change in daytime sleepiness was detected. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously, and larger prospective studies are needed to confirm them.
papers.journal: Journal of back and musculoskeletal rehabilitation

papers.title: Efficacy of High-Frequency Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Therapy for Depression With Insomnia Symptoms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Based on Randomized Controlled Trials.
papers.abstract: This meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy of high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (HF-rTMS) targeting the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) in patients with comorbid depression and insomnia. This analysis incorporated 7 studies, involving 709 subjects (control: 342; repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation [rTMS]: 367). All included studies employed left DLPFC-targeted HF-rTMS. Treatment effectiveness for comorbid depression and insomnia was assessed. Subgroup analyses were conducted to explore possible sources of heterogeneity. HF-rTMS significantly improved sleep quality (standardized mean difference [SMD] [95% confidence interval (CI)]: 0.97 [0.23 to 1.71], p = 0.01) and depressive symptoms (0.61 [0.38 to 0.84], p < 0.00001). There was a non-significant trend toward reduced sleep latency (0.50 [-0.17 to 1.18], p = 0.14). No significant difference in adverse reactions was observed (risk ratio [95% CI]: 1.09 [0.80 to 1.48], p = 0.57). Substantial heterogeneity was identified for the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index outcomes (I2 = 91%). Subgroup analyses indicated that this heterogeneity was attributed to variations in stimulation frequency and baseline antidepressant use. Very‑low to low certainty evidence suggests that left DLPFC‑targeted HF‑rTMS may improve sleep quality and depressive symptoms in patients with depression and insomnia symptoms, with a favorable safety profile. However, due to substantial heterogeneity and methodological limitations, these findings should be considered exploratory and warrant confirmation by future high‑quality trials.

papers.title: Health-promoting behaviors in perimenopausal women based on the COM-B model: a latent profile analysis.
papers.abstract: Perimenopause is a critical transitional stage in women's lives and is characterized by substantial physiological and psychological changes that may influence health behaviors and long-term health outcomes. Health-promoting behaviors play an important role in preventing chronic diseases and improving quality of life among perimenopausal women. However, these behaviors may vary considerably across individuals, and the psychosocial factors underlying different behavioral patterns remain unclear. Guided by the Capability-Opportunity-Motivation-Behaviors (COM-B) model, this study aimed to identify latent profiles of health-promoting behaviors among perimenopausal women and to examine their associated factors. This cross-sectional study included 500 women aged 40-55 years who were recruited by convenience sampling from the gynecology outpatient clinic of Dongguan Maternal and Child Health Hospital, China. Perimenopausal status was determined by a gynecologist with reference to STRAW + 10 menstrual criteria, defined as a persistent difference of at least 7 days in consecutive cycle lengths or an amenorrhea interval of at least 60 days but less than 12 months. Health-promoting behavior was assessed using the revised Chinese Health-Promoting Lifestyle Profile II. Latent profile analysis was conducted using six dimension scores. Theory-informed ordinal logistic regression examined associations of eHealth literacy, Family APGAR score, general self-efficacy, and prespecified covariates with profile level; a sensitivity model additionally adjusted for self-rated health, sleep quality, and body mass index category. Three ordered profiles of health-promoting behavior were identified: low-level (32.8%), moderate-level (46.4%), and high-level (20.8%). Their broadly parallel patterns across the six HPLP-II-R dimensions indicated primarily graded differences in overall health-promoting behavior. Higher eHealth literacy (OR = 1.266, 95% CI: 1.198-1.338), Family APGAR scores (OR = 1.137, 95% CI: 1.041-1.242), and general self-efficacy (OR = 1.125, 95% CI: 1.081-1.170) were associated with greater odds of membership in a higher-level profile. Health-promoting behaviors among perimenopausal women show substantial heterogeneity. Higher eHealth literacy, Family APGAR scores, and general self-efficacy-reflecting selected aspects of psychological capability, social opportunity, and reflective motivation within the COM-B framework-were associated with greater odds of membership in a higher-level health-promoting behavior profile. These may provide reference evidence for the importance of developing targeted health promotion strategies to support perimenopausal women in adopting healthier lifestyles.

papers.title: Elevated homocysteine and non-suicidal self-injury in adolescent depression: possible sex-specific clinical associations.
papers.abstract: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) has become increasingly prevalent among adolescents with major depressive disorder (MDD), yet its underlying biological mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study investigated the association between serum homocysteine and NSSI in adolescents with MDD, with emphasis on sex-specific effects. This retrospective study enrolled 141 adolescents with MDD, categorized into NSSI (n = 57) and Non-NSSI (NNSSI, n = 84) groups. Serum homocysteine was measured from fasting samples at admission. Clinical symptoms were assessed using the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD) and Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA). Analysis of covariance compared homocysteine between groups. Partial correlation and hierarchical regression analyses examined associations between homocysteine and clinical symptoms, evaluating sex moderation effects. Homocysteine was significantly elevated in the NSSI versus NNSSI group (14.57 ± 7.31 vs. 11.70 ± 2.77 µmol/L, P = 0.001). In the NNSSI group, homocysteine negatively correlated with diurnal variation (r = -0.232, P = 0.034). Hierarchical regression revealed distinct sex moderation patterns across groups. In the NNSSI group, significant sex-by-homocysteine interactions were identified for sleep disturbance (β = 0.376, P = 0.013) and somatic symptoms (β = 0.127, P = 0.019). In the NSSI group, interaction effects appeared only for diurnal variation (β = 0.056, P = 0.034). Elevated homocysteine may serve as a potential biological marker for NSSI in adolescents with MDD. Associations between homocysteine and clinical symptoms may exhibit sex-specific patterns that differed markedly between NSSI and NNSSI groups.
papers.journal: Child and adolescent psychiatry and mental health

papers.title: The role of BDNF, CREB, DAT, GFAP and Arc in manic- and OCD-like behavioral phenotypes in both sexes of rats exposed to REM sleep deprivation.
papers.abstract: Rapid-eye movement sleep deprivation (REM SD) has controversial effects on behavioral functions and cognitive abilities. Recent evidence has shown that REM SD in rats may lead to manic- and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)-like behaviors. The present study aimed to assess the effect of REM SD in both sexes of rats on locomotor activity, anxiety-like behavior, stereotyped behaviors, and OCD-like behavior. The possible role of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), cAMP response element-binding (CREB), dopamine transporter (DAT), glia fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), and activity-regulated cytoskeleton-associated protein (Arc) was also assessed using real-time PCR. REM SD was done for 14 days (6 h/d). Locomotor activity, anxiety-like behavior, grooming, and sniffing were measured using the open field test, and the marble burying test measured repetitive/compulsive-like responses. The results showed REM SD in both sexes led to hyperlocomotion, decreased anxiety, and increased OCD-like and stereotyped behaviors, with more effects in females except anxiety-like behavior. Also, the expression level of BDNF, CREB, DAT, and Arc was decreased and GFAP was increased in the hippocampus of both sexes of REM SD rats, with more effects in females except CREB. In conclusion, and for the first time, the present study showed the possible role of Arc, DAT, and GFAP in the induction of OCD- and manic-like behaviors and stereotyped behaviors in both sexes of rats. We also observed reduced BDNF and CREB expression in REM SD animals, suggesting a potential association between these molecular alterations and the behavioral changes induced by REM SD. Interventions targeting these molecular pathways could offer promising therapeutic strategies for REM SD-induced mood disorders.

papers.title: BTBD9-driven IMPDH2 ubiquitination governs sleep homeostasis by gating adenosine metabolism in the basal forebrain.
papers.abstract: BTB domain containing 9 (BTBD9) is among the most reproducible genetic risk factors for sleep-related disorders, yet its molecular function in sleep regulation remains unclear. Here, we aimed to define the downstream substrate, core brain region, and molecular mechanism through which BTBD9 regulates sleep-wake homeostasis. Population-scale genomic and brain expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) datasets were integrated to infer the direction of BTBD9-associated genetic risk in sleep-related traits. Basal forebrain-specific neuronal manipulation of Btbd9 was combined with electroencephalography/electromyography (EEG/EMG)-based sleep analysis and fiberphotomerty to define the relevant brain locus and functional output. Ubiquitinomics, protein interaction, ubiquitination, and enzymatic assays were used to identify BTBD9-regulated substrates and determine how BTBD9-dependent modification affects metabolic enzyme activity. Basal forebrain-specific genetic disruption, receptor pharmacology, and adeno-associated virus (AAV)-delivered interfering peptides were further applied to test pathway necessity and reversibility in vivo. human genetic analyses showed that BTBD9 variants associated with higher expression predicted a pro-arousal tendency. Consistently, neuron-specific deletion of Btbd9 in the mouse basal forebrain increased non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep and extracellular adenosine levels. Mechanistically, IMPDH2, the rate-limiting enzyme in de novo purine biosynthesis, was identified as a substrate of the Cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin ligase 3 (CRL3)BTBD9 ubiquitin ligase. BTBD9-mediated ubiquitination at IMPDH2 lysine 195 (K195) relieved guanosine triphosphate (GTP)-dependent allosteric inhibition, thereby limiting adenosine accumulation and sleep pressure. Basal forebrain neuronal knockout of Impdh2 recapitulated the sleep-promoting effect of Btbd9 deletion, whereas adenosine A1 receptor (A1R) blockade attenuated this phenotype. AAV-delivered interfering peptides targeting the BTBD9-IMPDH2 interaction reduced IMPDH2 ubiquitination, elevated adenosine levels, increased NREM sleep, and rescued BTBD9 overexpression-induced abnormal wakefulness in vivo. These findings identify a BTBD9-IMPDH2-adenosine pathway that links human genetic risk to basal forebrain control of sleep homeostasis. By defining BTBD9 as a molecular regulator of purine metabolism, this study provides a mechanistic framework for understanding and potentially targeting BTBD9-related sleep dysregulation.

papers.title: Today's flow, tomorrow's subjective well-being: temporal dynamics in the Chinese educational context.
papers.abstract: Optimal experience (flow) in academic study has been positively associated with student well-being; however, the precise day-to-day temporal ordering of this relationship remains to be empirically clarified. To advance this understanding, the present study examined within-person reciprocal associations between academic flow and subjective well-being among university students. A 21-day daily diary design was employed with 51 university students, yielding 1,006 valid daily observations and a compliance rate of 93.9%. Subjective well-being was assessed across three dimensions: positive affect, negative affect, and life satisfaction. Three Bayesian dynamic structural equation models were estimated to capture within-person dynamics, with daily sleep duration incorporated as a control variable. Significant within-person autoregressive effects were identified for all study variables. Daily academic flow prospectively predicted positive affect and life satisfaction on the following day, whereas neither well-being component predicted subsequent flow, indicating a unidirectional rather than reciprocal association. No longitudinal association was observed between flow and negative affect. These findings support the temporal precedence of academic flow in predicting daily subjective well-being, consistent with a eudaimonic perspective on student development. In practice, these results encourage educators and institutional practitioners to prioritize cultivating optimal learning experiences as a meaningful strategy to sustain student well-being in higher education.

papers.title: Self-compassion predicts reduced bedtime procrastination through affect pathway: a three-wave longitudinal study.
papers.abstract: Bedtime procrastination is a prevalent self-regulation failure phenomenon among college students, linked to poor sleep quality and mental illness. There are many factors contributing to bedtime procrastination. Among them, self-compassion may alleviate it through its influence on emotional states, yet few studies have researched in-depth on this mechanism. We conducted a three-wave longitudinal study with 7,174 Chinese college students (Mage = 19.11; 62.8% female) over an 8-month period. Self-compassion, positive affect, negative affect, and bedtime procrastination were measured at each wave. Cross-lagged panel modeling was used to examine temporal associations and indirect effects of self-compassion on bedtime procrastination through affective states. Significant correlations among self-compassion, positive affect, negative affect, and bedtime procrastination at different waves were observed (all p < 0.001). Self-compassion predicted reduced bedtime procrastination over time both directly (β = -0.051, p < 0.001) and indirectly via increased positive affect (β = -0.007, p < 0.001) and decreased negative affect (β = -0.005, p < 0.001). This study provides the first longitudinal evidence that both positive and negative affect mediate the association between self-compassion and bedtime procrastination. These findings support emotion regulation as a key mechanism linking self-compassion to adaptive sleep behavior. Enhancing self-compassion may be a promising target for interventions aimed at reducing bedtime procrastination and improving sleep health among university students.

papers.title: Astrocytes and memory: emerging evidence and a paradigm shift.
papers.abstract: In recent years, with the discovery of astrocytes as components of the tripartite synapse and the development of tools for manipulating astrocyte calcium events, learning and memory are no longer considered the exclusive domain of neurons; activation of astrocytes alone can also trigger memory recall. The mnemonic functions of astrocytes have now been demonstrated in the hippocampus, nucleus accumbens, and amygdala, and are mainly manifested during the memory retrieval phase. On the other hand, cooperation between astrocyte-derived gliotransmitters and memory engram neurons is crucial for the formation and consolidation of both short-term and long-term memory. For example, activation of astrocytic calcium signaling and stimulation by endocannabinoids can induce the release of D-serine, ATP/adenosine, and glutamate, which act on GPCR and thereby influence LTD or LTP. Among these molecules, lactate can also function as a signaling molecule to activate downstream memory processes, potentially involving D-serine- and NMDAR-mediated synaptic plasticity. Similarly, α1, α2, and β-adrenergic receptors, which are predominantly expressed in astrocytes, participate in memory in distinct ways across different brain regions. In addition, this review discusses the mechanisms by which astrocytes, as a medium for memory storage, participate in Alzheimer's disease, addictive behaviors, sleep disorders, depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder, as well as their therapeutic potential. Finally, this review systematically details the challenges and future directions in elucidating the mechanisms by which astrocytes store and process memory at the current stage, which may facilitate the development of novel astrocyte-targeted therapies for cognition-related disorders.

papers.title: Multidimensional predictors of psychological distress in dental education: the mediating role of academic stress a structural equation modelling study with competing model specification.
papers.abstract: Dental students experience disproportionately high levels of psychological distress, with prevalence rates of clinically significant stress ranging from 22 to 50% across international samples. Academic stress has been identified as the primary mediating pathway through which sociodemographic and lifestyle factors influence mental health outcomes. However, it remains unclear whether psychological distress in dental students is better represented by a transdiagnostic mental distress construct or by disorder-specific measures such as GAD-7 within structural equation modelling frameworks. This study aimed to test a structural equation model (SEM) in which sociodemographic and lifestyle factors predict psychological distress through the mediating role of academic stress, and to compare a transdiagnostic Mental Distress model (Model 1) with a GAD-7 anxiety-specific model (Model 2). A cross-sectional survey was administered to 303 dental students (years 1-5) in a Turkish dental school. Instruments included the Academic Stress Scale (ASÖ; 5 items), the GAD-7, and the DASS-21 (Depression and Anxiety subscales). Structural equation modelling was conducted in AMOS 24.0 with 5,000 bootstrap iterations and bias-corrected 95% confidence intervals. Both models demonstrated acceptable fit. Academic stress fully mediated the relationship between all examined predictors and psychological distress outcomes. Economic status emerged as the strongest predictor of academic stress, followed by gender and year of study. Poor sleep quality was associated with elevated academic stress. The competing model incorporating GAD-7 as an additional latent construct showed comparable fit, confirming the robustness of the mediation structure. Academic stress acts as a central full mediator between modifiable and sociodemographic factors and psychological distress in dental students. The transdiagnostic model offers superior theoretical fit, while the GAD-7 model provides practical clinical utility for early screening. Interventions targeting economic support, sleep hygiene, and routine GAD-7 screening are recommended.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning for identifying mild cognitive impairment among Chinese patients with obstructive sleep apnea: a multicenter cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is clinically relevant in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). We developed and externally validated an interpretable machine-learning model for concurrent clinically defined MCI to support prioritization for formal cognitive assessment rather than diagnosis. This multicenter cross-sectional diagnostic-prediction study included 400 eligible patients with OSA from Changchun, divided into a training set (n = 280) and an internal algorithm-selection hold-out (n = 120), plus an independent Shenzhen external-validation sample (n = 192). MCI classification integrated reported cognitive decline, objective cognitive evidence, largely preserved everyday independence, dementia exclusion, and assessment-team consensus with physician participation. Of 27 candidate predictors, redundancy review left 24 and LASSO-Boruta consensus retained nine. Feature selection was performed once on the full training set before repeated cross-validation and was not nested within resampling folds. Eight algorithms were tuned using repeated 10-fold cross-validation with training-fold-only SMOTE and PR-AUC as the primary metric. The RF threshold (0.3228) was derived from training out-of-fold probabilities and locked before validation. MCI was classified in 93/280 (33.2%), 38/120 (31.7%), and 57/192 (29.7%) participants. The nine RF predictors were coffee consumption, physical activity, AHI, MSaO2, PHQ-9, GAD-7, ESS, CPSS-14, and PSQI total scores. In the internal hold-out used for algorithm selection, RF achieved ROC-AUC 0.953, PR-AUC 0.936, and Brier score 0.060; these selection-conditioned estimates are not unbiased generalization estimates. In independent external validation, ROC-AUC was 0.957, PR-AUC 0.809, and Brier score 0.051. Calibration intercept - 0.616 and slope 0.701 indicated systematic probability overestimation despite strong discrimination. The RF model discriminated strongly in Shenzhen, but external miscalibration and systematic probability overestimation mean that high AUC does not make raw probabilities transportable; local calibration assessment and, if needed, recalibration are required before clinical use. The MCI outcome cannot be reproduced from questionnaire/scale scores alone, and Supplementary Table S10 is a retrospective operational specification rather than the original CRF. Performance evidence comes almost entirely from male OSA patients; validity in women is unestablished, and the model should not be used for clinical assessment in females. It is a research screening-prioritization tool, not a diagnostic, causal, prognostic, or clinical-impact instrument.

papers.title: Metabolic bridge between sleep disturbances and depression: mediating effects of insulin resistance and clinical implications.
papers.abstract: This study's objective was to investigate the mediating role of insulin resistance (IR) in the association between sleep disturbances and depression and reveal its underlying biological mechanisms and clinical implications. The present study's sample population was derived from data collected during the period of 2005 to 2014 as part of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. The total sample size comprised 20,510 adults. The utilization of multidimensional sleep assessment (sleep duration, trouble sleeping, and sleep disorders), the PHQ-9 depression scale, and clinically validated IR indicators (METS-IR, TyG, and TyG-BMI) was undertaken to parse associations between variables and quantify mediating effects. This was accomplished by constructing multivariable adjusted modeling, restricted cubic spline modeling, causal-mediation analytic frameworks, and using multiple imputation techniques to address missing data. The results of the study indicated a significant association between sleep disturbances and depression. Sleep disturbances were defined as trouble sleeping, sleep disorders, and poor sleep patterns. Additionally, there was a significant positive association between IR indicators and depression. Following the implementation of confounder adjustment, a unit increase in METS-IR was associated with a 2% increase in the prevalence of depression (OR = 1.02, 95% CI: 1.01-1.02). The ORs for TyG and TyG-BMI were 1.36 (95% CI: 1.26-1.45) and 1.01 (95% CI: 1.01-1.01), respectively. The relationship between sleep disturbances and depression was partially mediated by IR, with mediation ratios ranging from 1.94% to 7.34%. The most substantial mediating effect (7.34%) was observed for TyG-BMI. Furthermore, it was observed that individuals with poorer sleep quality exhibited an elevated prevalence of IR and depression (P for trend < 0.001). The mediating effect of IR indicators remained significant after multiple imputations were used to address missing variables. IR constitutes a significant biological mechanism that links sleep disturbances to depression. The enhancement of sleep quality and the regulation of IR may be pivotal in preventing and managing depression. Future studies should further validate the causality and mechanism of this relationship and explore effective interventions. Not applicable.

papers.title: Adaptation and validation for Chilean Spanish of the checklist individual strength (CIS) in Chilean workers.
papers.abstract: Work fatigue (WF) is a complex physical and mental exhaustion caused by multiple factors. It is a growing occupational and health phenomenon in contemporary society. Thus, there is a need for validated and adapted instruments in different languages for an adequate assessment of this pressing public health problem. In this study the psychometric properties of the original Anglo-American version of the 20-item CIS were examined in 686 Chilean workers in the security and education employment sectors (Spanish Latin American version). A 16-item version (CIS-16R) was obtained, with adequate reliability (Cronbach's alpha of 0.93 and 0.86) and content validity (r = .76 with the 3D-WFI). Four of its original items were eliminated, as they needed to exceed the item-total correlation cut-off point adequately. An exploratory factor analysis yielded a bi-factor structure (and not four as in its original version), which we named general and physical fatigue, respectively. The Spanish-adapted version of the CIS is proposed. In addition, the weight of job demands and other ergonomic and environmental variables in generating WF were identified. Among the effects of WF, self-assessments of reduced health, higher absenteeism, lower job satisfaction, and lower sleep quality were observed.

papers.title: Neural mechanisms of cognitive dysfunction in depression: dual-task event-related potentials and task-phase-dependent EEG functional connectivity.
papers.abstract: To investigate the neurophysiological features underlying depression-related cognitive dysfunction via dual-task event-related potential (ERP) and task-phase-dependent electroencephalography (EEG) functional connectivity analysis. Thirty patients with depression (DP group) and 30 matched healthy controls (HC group) underwent EEG recordings across pre-task resting state, face perception task (indexed by N170), face mismatch conflict monitoring task (indexed by N270), and post-task resting state. Functional connectivity was quantified using imaginary coherence (iCoh), with between-group comparisons corrected by Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR). Correlation analyses between electrophysiological metrics and clinical variables were performed in the DP group. The DP group exhibited prolonged latency and decreased amplitude of N170, prolonged latency and increased amplitude of N270, as well as task-phase-dependent multi-frequency brain network imbalances. In the DP group, longer N170 and N270 latencies were associated with more severe depressive symptoms, whereas task-phase-dependent functional connectivity abnormalities showed no significant associations with clinical variables. Depression was associated with electrophysiological abnormalities in emotional processing and conflict monitoring, as well as task-phase-dependent brain network imbalances, providing exploratory neurophysiological evidence related to depression-associated cognitive dysfunction. Not applicable.

papers.title: The impact of work-related foot pain on work and personal life: an interview study.
papers.abstract: The occurrence of foot pain is high, especially in those with physically demanding occupations. Work-related foot pain has been shown to impact work performance, family life, and leisure activities. While prevalence across various sectors is documented, research exploring experiences and total life impact of work-related foot pain remains limited. The aim of this study was to explore experiences of living with foot pain among individuals employed in highly demanding physical occupations, and occupations characterised by prolonged standing or walking. A qualitative, semi-structured interview-based approach was chosen. Twelve individual interviews were conducted with nine women and three men, and analysed using Qualitative Content Analysis. One main theme, Walking a fine line - Balancing challenges in multiple aspects of life due to work-related foot pain, and three sub-themes were identified, describing how external work-environment factors and internal experiences of autonomy impact an individual's overall life situation, including impact on family life and the mental toll of living and working with foot pain. The sub-theme Struggling with increased pain due to work conditions and environment highlights how factors such as certain types of floors, physical work demands, time spent on the feet, walking, heavy lifting, and inadequate footwear directly exacerbate pain. The sub-theme Feeling like just another cog in the machine due to limited control over workplace organisation reflects difficulties for employees in influencing work tasks, planning daily work tasks and responsibilities, a lack of recovery during the workday, and communication within the workplace. The sub-theme Experiencing inequality and low quality of life outside of work describes the consequences for individuals' personal lives, including restricted social participation, strained family relations, negative emotions, and sleep disturbances. Overall, the individuals expressed a sense of resignation, feeling that they had to "grit their teeth" and continue working despite the pain. The central findings of this study are negative experiences and struggles, during both work and leisure time. Understanding the experiences of individuals with work-related foot pain can help employers and healthcare providers to identify work-related risks and consider preventative measures, although further research on this topic is needed. Not applicable.

papers.title: Sleep quality, circadian rhythm disruption, functioning, and treatment adherence in major depression: a cross-sectional exploratory study.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances and circadian rhythm disruption are highly prevalent in major depressive disorder (MDD) and may contribute to poorer functioning and reduced treatment adherence. However, few studies have examined sleep quality, biological rhythm disruption, functioning, and medication adherence concurrently in an outpatient depression sample. This study investigated the relationships among sleep quality, biological rhythm, functional status, medication adherence, and depression severity in patients diagnosed with depression. A descriptive, correlational cross-sectional study was conducted in the Adult Psychiatry Outpatient Clinic of Maltepe University Faculty of Medicine Hospital between 16 December 2024 and 15 March 2025. A total of 110 patients with a confirmed diagnosis of depression were included. Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), biological rhythm disruption using the Biological Rhythm Interview of Assessment in Neuropsychiatry (BRIAN), functional status using the Social Functioning Scale (SFS-T), medication adherence using the Medication Adherence Rating Scale (MARS), and depression severity using the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI). Pearson correlation analyses were used to examine associations among variables, and multiple linear regression analyses were conducted to identify independent factors associated with sleep quality. Sleep impairment was common: 46.4% of participants reported moderate sleep quality and 31.8% reported poor sleep quality. Mean PSQI score was 8.31 (SD = 4.21). Poorer sleep quality (higher PSQI scores) was moderately associated with lower social functioning (r = - 0.300, p < 0.01) and lower medication adherence (r = - 0.350, p < 0.01), and strongly associated with greater biological rhythm disruption (r = 0.621, p < 0.01). Sleep quality was also positively correlated with depression severity (r = 0.494, p < 0.01). Sleep impairment was common: 46.4% of participants reported moderate sleep quality and 31.8% reported poor sleep quality. Poorer sleep quality (higher PSQI scores) was moderately associated with lower social functioning (r = - 0.300, p < 0.01) and lower medication adherence (r = - 0.350, p < 0.01), and positively associated with biological rhythm disruption (r = 0.621, p < 0.01) and depressive symptom severity (r = 0.494, p < 0.01). In the multiple linear regression analysis, the overall model was statistically significant (R² = 0.429, p < 0.001), explaining 42.9% of the variance in sleep quality. After adjustment for the other variables, biological rhythm disruption remained the only independent predictor of sleep quality (β = 0.445, p < 0.001). In this outpatient depression sample, poor sleep quality was significantly associated with circadian rhythm disruption, reduced functioning, lower medication adherence, and greater depressive symptom severity. These findings support the clinical value of early sleep screening and integrated approaches that address sleep-circadian regulation alongside functional recovery, with possible benefits for treatment engagement in outpatient mental health care. Not applicable.

papers.title: Structural brain age gap and clinical determinants in migraine: a cross-sectional MRI study.
papers.abstract: Migraine has been linked to structural brain alterations that may deviate from normative aging patterns. Recent brain-age modeling studies have reported elevated brain age gap (BAG) values in migraine populations, but the clinical factors associated with individual variation in BAG remain incompletely characterized. This study quantified BAG in patients with migraine and identified demographic, lifestyle, and clinical factors independently associated with structural brain-age deviation. This cross-sectional study enrolled 128 patients with migraine (ICHD-3 criteria) and 35 non-migraine controls. Brain age was estimated using a support vector regression model trained on T1-weighted MRI scans from an independent multicenter dataset of 1,410 healthy adults. The primary outcome was the bias-corrected BAG. Multivariable linear regression analysis identified independent predictors of BAG within the migraine cohort across headache, psychiatric, sleep, and lifestyle domains. An exploratory extreme-group comparison contrasted migraine patients in the upper and lower BAG tertiles using binary logistic regression. Patients with migraine exhibited a significantly higher bias-corrected BAG than controls (9.76 ± 8.97 vs. 4.88 ± 8.25 years; ANCOVA adjusted for age, age², and total intracranial volume: F = 6.795, p = 0.010, partial η²=0.041). In multivariable linear regression analysis, depressive symptom severity (Beck Depression Inventory-II [BDI-II]: β = 0.39, 95% CI = 0.03-0.75, p = 0.033) was independently associated with a larger BAG. Current smoking was also independently associated with a larger BAG (β = 7.56, 95% CI = 0.63-14.48, p = 0.033), although this estimate was based on only 10 current smokers and should be interpreted with caution. In the exploratory extreme-group analysis, higher depressive symptoms (BDI-II, OR = 1.24, 95% CI = 1.04-1.49, p = 0.019) were associated with the high-aging phenotype. Headache frequency, disease duration, and aura status showed no significant association with BAG in any analysis. Migraine was associated with a significantly higher structural BAG relative to non-migraine controls. Within the migraine cohort, depressive symptom burden was the most consistent clinical correlate of BAG, whereas current smoking emerged as a preliminary lifestyle signal requiring confirmation in cohorts with more current smokers. These findings suggest that structural brain-age deviation in migraine is associated with psychiatric and lifestyle factors beyond headache-specific characteristics, supporting further longitudinal research into potentially modifiable clinical correlates.
papers.journal: The journal of headache and pain

papers.title: Perceptions of older adults on chronic pain management in primary care settings.
papers.abstract: Chronic pain disproportionately affects older adults (age ≥ 65 years), and almost half of the United States older adult population reports chronic pain. Chronic pain is associated with decreased physical function and impairs activities of daily living. Improving Chicago Older Adult Opioid and Pain Management through Patient-centered Clinical Decision Support and Project ECHO® (I-COPE) was designed to develop effective pain management by studying patient goals, preferences, and comorbidities. I-COPE collects patient-reported data, implements clinical decision support tools, and provides primary care clinician education on evidence-based chronic pain treatments. To explore the perspectives of older adults receiving chronic pain management in primary care and their views on I-COPE. I-COPE was implemented at 36 clinics within two healthcare systems in Chicago metropolitan area. Patients who met study criteria were invited to participate in semi-structured interviews. Sixteen older adult patients with a high pain score, chronic pain, or opioid use disorder in the last year. Patients were interviewed about their experiences with chronic pain management and their opinions about I-COPE until theme saturation was reached. Participants described the effects of chronic pain, impacting mobility, daily activities, sleep, relationships, and wellbeing. Participants desired improved daily functioning, pain, and independence. They preferred treatments that increased physical activity, limited medications, and were not surgeries/procedures. During treatment decision-making, patients considered clinician recommendations, their goals, and current/past treatment effectiveness. Pain management satisfaction was associated with elements of shared decision making. Overall, participants believed that I-COPE tools could enhance clinician understanding of pain. Older adult patients with chronic pain share pain management goals and treatment preferences similar to those reported in studies of primary care clinicians. Greater satisfaction with pain management was associated with shared decision-making principles. Patients held favorable opinions towards I-COPE in addressing barriers to pain management. The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov under #NCT04878562 on May 4, 2021.

papers.title: Association between PM2.5 and its chemical components exposure and heart disease risk: a longitudinal study from China.
papers.abstract: Air pollution, particularly fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and its chemical components, poses a significant threat to public health. However, the association between these pollutants and heart disease risk, have not been thoroughly investigated, especially regarding differential effects across various populations and regions. we analysed 8,172 participants from 123 cities across China. Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to assess the association between PM2.5 and its major chemical components (sulfate [SO₄²⁻], nitrate [NO₃⁻], ammonium [NH₄⁺], organic matter [OM], and black carbon [BC]) with heart disease risk. We constructed three progressively adjusted models, employed Weighted Quantile Sum regression to evaluate the composite effects of pollutant mixtures, used restricted cubic splines to explore dose-response relationships, and calculated Population Attributable Fraction. Additionally, stratified analyses were conducted to explore effect modification by age, gender, body mass index (BMI), residence, geographic region, smoking status, and drinking status. The study found significant associations between PM2.5 and all its major chemical components with heart disease risk (p < 0.001). In the fully adjusted model (Model 3, adjusted for age, gender, body mass index, marital status, retirement status, residence, geographic region, education level, sleep duration, smoking, and drinking), each 1 µg/m³ increase in PM2.5 concentration was associated with a 2.7% increase in heart disease risk (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.027, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.022-1.032). Among the chemical components, BC showed the largest estimate per 1 µg/m³ increase associated with a 38.1% increase in risk (HR = 1.381, 95% CI: 1.266-1.506). All pollutants exhibited non-linear dose-response relationships with heart disease risk (p for nonlinear < 0.001). Geographic region and BMI were important effect modifiers, with southern residents and overweight individuals showing increased stronger associations to air pollution-related heart disease risks. The PAF of heart disease due to PM2.5 was 2.63%. PM2.5 and its chemical components are significantly associated with heart disease risk, with notable differences in impact magnitude across components. BC showed the strongest association with heart disease risk. Southern residents and overweight individuals showed increased stronger associations to air pollution-related heart disease risks.
